title: Findings
heading: Findings

verdict.heading: Black Giant page: EnergyX → this demo
verdict.summary: {fact:lh-bg-video-total} of {fact:lh-bg-weight} is two video files. The rest of the page — design, images, code — is {fact:lh-bg-other-bytes}.

intro: The whole argument on one page: what EnergyX's pages transfer and why, what this demo changes, what it cannot prove, and what the fact registry turned up. Every figure links to its source.

timeline.heading: What that wait looks like
timeline.intro: Both phones replay the measured lab timings at real speed: the first paint, then the largest element on the screen, the thing a visitor came for.
timeline.caption: A visualisation of the measured Lighthouse lab figures, not a recording of either page.

payload.heading: Where the bytes go
body: EnergyX's Black Giant page transfers {fact:lh-bg-weight} on a first visit. Of that, {fact:lh-bg-video-total} is two video files. Everything else on the page together comes to {fact:lh-bg-other-bytes}.

So the page is not heavy because it is rich. The design, copy and images are a small slice of the total. The weight is two finished videos reaching the browser as large single downloads, because there is no delivery step between the footage and the page. The homepage has the same shape.

parts.label: Hero video, via a Box shared link

payload.scaleNote: Bars share one scale, so their lengths compare directly. Solid segments are video; lighter segments are everything else.

comparison.heading: Before and after
comparison.intro: The Black Giant page as EnergyX serves it, and as this demo delivers it: a still poster first, video only after the page has loaded.
comparison.caption: Lighthouse lab results, Black Giant page
comparison.method: Both columns use the same settings: Lighthouse 13.5.0, mobile, emulated Moto G Power on Slow 4G throttling, first visit. Each figure links to its report.

caveats.heading: What these numbers do not show
points: The video on this demo's Black Giant page is a placeholder: a short public-domain NASA clip, not EnergyX's footage. EnergyX's hero file alone is {fact:lh-bg-hero-video}. The placeholder is far smaller, so this demo's total says nothing about how small EnergyX's own video would be once prepared for the web.

Deferring the video fixes the Largest Contentful Paint: the first screen no longer waits for a video. It does not reduce the bytes. A phone that goes on to play the video still downloads all of it. Cutting the payload takes re-encoding, at sizes and in formats made for phones. That is the second half of the fix, and it has not been done here on EnergyX's files.

All of this is lab data: Lighthouse on one emulated phone over a throttled connection. It is repeatable, which makes it useful for before and after, but it is not what real visitors experience. Field data from real devices could be better or worse, and single Lighthouse runs vary from run to run.
This demo's figures are from the US West test region, because that is the region the EnergyX measurement ran in. US East scored higher and is not used.

registry.heading: What the registry found
registry.intro: Putting every published figure in one place, each with what it counts, surfaced two cases worth a look. Neither means a published figure is off. Both are about what a figure says it measures.

cases.heading: Days or hours: one process, two published timings
body: The homepage comparison table gives the DLE processing time as {fact:ex-dle-time}. The FAQ on the same page says hours.
Both can be accurate if they measure different spans of the process. Neither says which span it measures, so a retail investor, or a model summarising the page, cannot tell them apart.

cases.heading: Water: the claim undersells EnergyX's own figures
body: The homepage FAQ says DLE cuts freshwater use by {fact:ex-water-reduction}. The same FAQ gives the figures behind it: {fact:ex-water-conventional} for conventional extraction, and {fact:ex-water-dle} for EnergyX's process. Those two figures work out to a reduction of {fact:ex-water-implied-reduction}.
The published claim is accurate, just far more modest than the figures beside it. This is the one case where making the figures agree makes EnergyX's claim stronger.

firstWeek.heading: First week on your codebase
firstWeek.intro: If I joined, this is what the first week would look like, in plain terms. None of it changes how the site looks.
points: Measure real visitors' phones alongside the lab numbers, and judge every change by both.
Add a video delivery step: phone-sized, re-encoded video, with no change for the people making it.
Gate each release on performance budgets (Lighthouse CI) and accessibility tests (axe).
Start one registry for every public figure, so each number changes in one place.
Generate llms.txt from it, so AI tools quote the same figures and refer forward-looking questions to IR.
